# Chiral-symmetry forcing of protected transfer eigenvalues (T1)

DRAFT (kernel-clean; no `s o r r y`). The K6 target of the overnight
all-mass run (2026-07-08), redirected by the determinant-parity probe

forced by cyclic symmetry - abstract winding-1 symmetric data is UNPINNED
(min|ev - 1| ~ 0.2-0.45), and equivariant-but-unpinned cases are common.

with `Gamma W Gamma = W^dagger`. Numerically this `Gamma` is the
orientation-swap, i.e. the edge-orientation-reversal grading - the SAME
grading that gives the exact Ginsparg-Wilson structure
(`GWRetardedTransfer.lean`). It is present exactly for the even-V
half-winding (alternating-phase) decoration and there pins BOTH `+1` and
`-1` in `spec(W)` for every hop amplitude `|t|` (probe: V = 4, 6, 8).

## What this module proves (the honest kernel core)

For a unitary `W` carrying such a chiral involution:

* `chiral_det_conj`: `det W` is real (`conj (det W) = det W`);
* `chiral_det_sq_one`: `(det W)^2 = 1`;
* `chiral_det_eq_pm_one`: hence `det W = 1` or `det W = -1`.

Since `det W = (-1)^{mult(-1)}` up to conjugate-pair factors, the sign of
`det W` fixes the PARITY of the `-1`-eigenvalue multiplicity - the honest
core of the determinant-parity mechanism (SevenChallenges memo finding 8).
The full `|t|`-independent DOUBLE pinning (both `+-1` always present at
even dimension) needs the chiral winding invariant (Asboth-Obuse `Z x Z`
for chiral discrete-time walks, arXiv:1303.1199) and is left at oracle
grade - see the probe and `SEVENCHALLENGES_ANALYSIS.md`.

## Claim boundary

eigenvalue-multiplicity reading is stated in prose, not in a theorem.
No continuum, no physical-mode claim beyond the finite determinant fact.

## Provenance

Mechanism identified by the overnight K6 probe (2026-07-08); the chiral
`Gamma U Gamma = U^dagger` structure and its `0/pi`-mode consequences are
standard for chiral-symmetric quantum walks (Asboth-Obuse 2013,
arXiv:1303.1199, in the paper graph) - [import]/[comp]. The edge-reversal
identification is this program's (`GWRetardedTransfer.lean`) - [orig].
-/

import Mathlib

namespace PhysicsSM.Draft.NullEdge.Carrier.ChiralZeroModeParity

open Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- A **chiral involution** for `W`: a self-inverse `Gamma` conjugating `W`
to its adjoint. For unitary `W` (`Wᴴ * W = 1`) this says `Gamma` conjugates
`W` to `W⁻¹` - the reciprocal-pairing (chiral) symmetry. -/
structure ChiralInvolution (W Gamma : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop where
  invol : Gamma * Gamma = 1
  chiral : Gamma * W * Gamma = Wᴴ

/-- Under a chiral involution, `det Gamma` squares to one. -/
theorem chiral_detGamma_sq {W Gamma : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (h : ChiralInvolution W Gamma) : Gamma.det * Gamma.det = 1 := by
  rw [← Matrix.det_mul, h.invol, Matrix.det_one]

/-- **`det W` is real** under a chiral involution: `conj (det W) = det W`.
(Taking `det` of `Gamma W Gamma = Wᴴ` and using `det Gamma ^2 = 1`.) -/
theorem chiral_det_conj {W Gamma : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (h : ChiralInvolution W Gamma) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) W.det = W.det := by
  have hdet : Gamma.det * W.det * Gamma.det = (Wᴴ).det := by
    rw [← Matrix.det_mul, ← Matrix.det_mul, h.chiral]
  rw [Matrix.det_conjTranspose] at hdet
  -- LHS = det W * (det Gamma)^2 = det W
  have hcomm : Gamma.det * W.det * Gamma.det
      = W.det * (Gamma.det * Gamma.det) := by ring
  rw [hcomm, chiral_detGamma_sq h, mul_one] at hdet
  exact hdet.symm

/-- Under a chiral involution with `W` unitary, `(det W)^2 = 1`. -/
theorem chiral_det_sq_one {W Gamma : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (h : ChiralInvolution W Gamma) (hU : Wᴴ * W = 1) :
    W.det * W.det = 1 := by
  -- |det W|^2 = 1 from unitarity, and det W real from the chiral symmetry
  have hmod : (starRingEnd ℂ) W.det * W.det = 1 := by
    have : (Wᴴ * W).det = 1 := by rw [hU, Matrix.det_one]
    rwa [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_conjTranspose] at this
  rw [chiral_det_conj h] at hmod
  exact hmod

/-- **The chiral determinant dichotomy (T1 core).** A unitary `W` carrying
a chiral involution has `det W = 1` or `det W = -1`. The sign fixes the
parity of the `-1`-eigenvalue multiplicity: the honest kernel core of the
determinant-parity forcing of protected `+-1` transfer modes. -/
theorem chiral_det_eq_pm_one {W Gamma : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (h : ChiralInvolution W Gamma) (hU : Wᴴ * W = 1) :
    W.det = 1 ∨ W.det = -1 := by
  have hsq : W.det * W.det = 1 := chiral_det_sq_one h hU
  have : (W.det - 1) * (W.det + 1) = 0 := by
    have : (W.det - 1) * (W.det + 1) = W.det * W.det - 1 := by ring
    rw [this, hsq, sub_self]
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp this with h1 | h2
  · exact Or.inl (by linear_combination h1)
  · exact Or.inr (by linear_combination h2)

end PhysicsSM.Draft.NullEdge.Carrier.ChiralZeroModeParity

```

/-
# S1-CC: closure is balanced (not positive) on the physical sector

DRAFT (kernel-clean; no `s o r r y`). The kernel core of the Fable call-01
resolution of the central positivity crux (S1-CC), overnight all-mass run
2026-07-08. The full analysis is in the call log
(`AgentTasks/model-calls/claude/2026-07-07-231939-fable-call-01.md`,
Part B) and summarized in the QCD roadmap.

## The finding (grade MEMO for the physics, M for this file)

The nonabelian closure channel is an exact Krein square `Q_C = L^# L`
(kernel-checked elsewhere), but Krein squares carry no positivity. The
crux "is closure positive on the physical sector `V'/N`?" is resolved:
**no - it is exactly BALANCED (Krein signature zero), structurally.** The
mechanism is a grading anticonjugation: the closure bivector
`b = sigma_z (x) 1` satisfies `b^{-1} (J Q_C) b = -(J Q_C)` and preserves
every gauge-defined constraint sector (gauge acts on the color/site factor
alone, commuting with `b`). A matrix congruent to its own negative has
balanced inertia (`n_+ = n_-`). So closure positivity holds only vacuously
(flat Gauss sector); otherwise the channel is honestly signed - which is
exactly what chiral symmetry breaking needs (§8 of the manuscript).

## What this file proves (the house-style rung)

`anticonj_odd_pow_trace_zero`: if an invertible `S` anticonjugates `B`
(`S^{-1} B S = -B`), then every ODD power of `B` is traceless. This is the
spectral-symmetry engine behind the balanced inertia: all odd moments of
the Hermitian form vanish, so its eigenvalues are symmetric about zero. A
pure finite trace identity in the same register as `banks_casher_count` -
no inertia API, no spectral theorem. The inertia reading itself (via
`charpoly` congruence and Sylvester) and the concrete `V'` construction
are the next rungs (see the roadmap); this is the load-bearing algebra.

## Claim boundary

`anticonj_odd_pow_trace_zero` is kernel-checked (M). The identification of
`B = J Q_C` and `S = b` on the concrete carrier physical sector, and the
step from odd-moment-vanishing to balanced inertia, are MEMO (Fable Part
B), pending their own Lean rungs. No positivity is claimed; the point is

## Provenance

Fable-5 call-01 (2026-07-08), Part B - the crux resolution and the
recommended house-style rung - [orig]/[interp]; the trace-conjugation and
odd-power algebra is standard - [import].
-/

import Mathlib

namespace PhysicsSM.Draft.NullEdge.GateYM.S1CCBalancedInertia

open Matrix

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- Trace is invariant under conjugation by an invertible matrix:
`Tr(S⁻¹ X S) = Tr X`. -/
theorem trace_invOf_conj (S X : Matrix n n ℂ) [Invertible S] :
    (⅟S * X * S).trace = X.trace := by
  rw [Matrix.trace_mul_comm, ← mul_assoc, mul_invOf_self, one_mul]

/-- Conjugation distributes over powers: `(S⁻¹ B S)^m = S⁻¹ B^m S`. -/
theorem conj_pow (S B : Matrix n n ℂ) [Invertible S] (m : ℕ) :
    (⅟S * B * S) ^ m = ⅟S * B ^ m * S := by
  induction m with
  | zero => simp
  | succ m ih =>
    rw [pow_succ, ih, pow_succ]
    have hreassoc : (⅟S * B ^ m * S) * (⅟S * B * S)
        = ⅟S * B ^ m * (S * ⅟S) * B * S := by noncomm_ring
    rw [hreassoc, mul_invOf_self, mul_one]
    noncomm_ring

/-- **Anticonjugation kills odd-power traces (S1-CC flagship).** If an
invertible `S` anticonjugates `B` (`S⁻¹ * B * S = -B`), then every odd
power of `B` is traceless: `Tr(B^(2k+1)) = 0`. The odd moments of the
associated Hermitian form all vanish, forcing a spectrum symmetric about
zero - the engine behind the BALANCED Krein inertia of the closure channel
on the physical sector (closure is signed, not positive). -/
theorem anticonj_odd_pow_trace_zero (B S : Matrix n n ℂ) [Invertible S]
    (h : ⅟S * B * S = -B) (k : ℕ) :
    (B ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace = 0 := by
  have h1 : ((-B) ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace = (B ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace := by
    rw [← h, conj_pow, trace_invOf_conj]
  have h2 : ((-B) ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace = -(B ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace := by
    rw [Odd.neg_pow ⟨k, rfl⟩, Matrix.trace_neg]
  have key : -(B ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace = (B ^ (2 * k + 1)).trace := h2 ▸ h1
  linear_combination (-(1 : ℂ) / 2) * key

/-- **Even-power form of the same fact:** for a self-adjoint `B` (`Bᴴ = B`)
that is anticonjugate to itself, the anticonjugation gives a spectrum
symmetric under negation. Recorded as the companion identity: `Tr B = 0`
(the `k = 0` case), the vanishing of the first moment. -/
theorem anticonj_trace_zero (B S : Matrix n n ℂ) [Invertible S]
    (h : ⅟S * B * S = -B) : B.trace = 0 := by
  have := anticonj_odd_pow_trace_zero B S h 0
  simpa using this

/-- **Spectrum symmetric under negation (the balanced-inertia essence).**
Anticonjugation `⅟S * B * S = -B` makes `B` similar to `-B`, so their
characteristic polynomials agree: `(-B).charpoly = B.charpoly`. Hence the
eigenvalue multiset of `B` is invariant under `lambda -> -lambda` - the
polynomial-level statement that the spectrum is symmetric about zero, from
which `n_+ = n_-` (balanced Krein inertia) follows for Hermitian `B` by
counting. This is the charpoly rung of the balanced-inertia theorem. -/
theorem anticonj_charpoly_eq (B S : Matrix n n ℂ) [Invertible S]
    (h : ⅟S * B * S = -B) : (-B).charpoly = B.charpoly := by
  rw [← h]
  exact Matrix.charpoly_units_conj' (unitOfInvertible S) B

/-! ## Count helper for the balanced-inertia capstone -/

/-- A real multiset invariant under negation has as many positive entries as
negative entries, counted with multiplicity.

This is the finite combinatorial half of the balanced-inertia capstone. The
remaining spectral bridge is to prove that the Hermitian eigenvalue multiset is
negation-invariant from the characteristic-polynomial symmetry. -/
theorem countP_pos_eq_countP_neg_of_map_neg_eq (s : Multiset ℝ)
    (h : s.map Neg.neg = s) :
    s.countP (fun x => 0 < x) = s.countP (fun x => x < 0) := by
  calc
    s.countP (fun x => 0 < x) = (s.map Neg.neg).countP (fun x => 0 < x) := by
      rw [h]
    _ = s.countP (fun x => 0 < -x) := by
      rw [Multiset.countP_map]
      simp [Multiset.countP_eq_card_filter]
    _ = s.countP (fun x => x < 0) := by
      apply Multiset.countP_congr rfl
      intro x _
      simp

/-- Index-count form of `countP_pos_eq_countP_neg_of_map_neg_eq`.

If the multiset of real values indexed by a finite type is invariant under
negation, the number of positive indexed values equals the number of negative
indexed values. This matches the count shape needed for Hermitian eigenvalues. -/
theorem card_pos_eq_card_neg_of_multiset_map_neg_eq {m : Type*} [Fintype m]
    (f : m → ℝ)
    (h : (Finset.univ.val.map f).map Neg.neg = Finset.univ.val.map f) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => 0 < f i)).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i < 0)).card := by
  have hm := countP_pos_eq_countP_neg_of_map_neg_eq (Finset.univ.val.map f) h
  have hpos : (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => 0 < f i)).card =
      (Finset.univ.val.map f).countP (fun x => 0 < x) := by
    rw [Multiset.countP_eq_card_filter, Multiset.filter_map]
    change (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => 0 < f i)).val.card = _
    rw [Finset.filter_val]
    simp
  have hneg : (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i < 0)).card =
      (Finset.univ.val.map f).countP (fun x => x < 0) := by
    rw [Multiset.countP_eq_card_filter, Multiset.filter_map]
    change (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i < 0)).val.card = _
    rw [Finset.filter_val]
    simp
  rw [hpos, hneg]
  exact hm

/-! ## Lemma 1: the half-constraint rigidity (Gupta-Bleuler is forced) -/

/-- **Half-constraint rigidity (Fable call-01, Part B, Lemma 1).** For the
null pair `c₁ = E₀₁`, `c₂ = E₁₀` on the Clifford factor, a two-covector
constraint charge `Q = c₁ ⊗ G₁ + c₂ ⊗ G₂` (here the `2x2`-over-`B` matrix
`!![0, G₁; G₂, 0]`) is nilpotent iff `G₁ G₂ = 0` AND `G₂ G₁ = 0`. So a
NILPOTENT (BRST-type) Gauss charge on the hyperbolic pair cannot use both
null covectors nontrivially: the Gupta-Bleuler "impose only half the
constraint" is not a modeling choice - it is FORCED by nilpotency.
(`Q² = !![G₁G₂, 0; 0, G₂G₁]`.) -/
theorem half_constraint_rigidity {B : Type*} [Ring B] (G₁ G₂ : B) :
    (!![0, G₁; G₂, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) B) ^ 2 = 0
      ↔ G₁ * G₂ = 0 ∧ G₂ * G₁ = 0 := by
  have hsq : (!![0, G₁; G₂, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) B)
      * !![0, G₁; G₂, 0] = !![G₁ * G₂, 0; 0, G₂ * G₁] := by
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two]
  rw [sq, hsq]
  constructor
  · intro hQ
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · have := congrFun (congrFun hQ 0) 0; simpa using this
    · have := congrFun (congrFun hQ 1) 1; simpa using this
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [h1, h2]

end PhysicsSM.Draft.NullEdge.GateYM.S1CCBalancedInertia

## Part B — the C4 invariant: it is NOT a global winding number; it is a reflection-sectored two-involution trace index

**Headline finding (verified today, machine precision, V = 4, 6, 8, |t| ∈ {0.3,…,0.9}):** for the half-winding decoration the **global** Asboth–Obuse-type index *vanishes* — `tr Γ = 0`, `tr(ΓW) = 0`, `ν₀ = ν_π = 0` — while `mult(+1) = mult(−1) = 2`. So no global invariant (winding, det parity, Pfaffian, Clifford `ℤ₂`) can force this pinning; the docstring line in `ChiralZeroModeParity.lean` attributing the double pinning to "the chiral winding invariant (Asboth-Obuse Z x Z)" is a MEMO-level misattribution and should be corrected. The protection is **equivariant**: `W` commutes exactly with the reflection-plus-orientation-swap `R` (legs `ℓ → −ℓ`, orientations swapped; `R² = 1`, `[R,Γ] = 0`), and the two `R`-sectors carry **opposite** chiral indices `(+1,+1)` and `(−1,−1)`, which cancel globally but pin one `+1` and one `−1` mode *each*.

### (a) Definition — the sectored chiral index (grade: M-target; definition is pure traces)

Data: `W` unitary (`Wᴴ W = 1`), `Γ` with `Γ² = 1`, `Γ W Γ = Wᴴ` (the repo's `ChiralInvolution` — note Hermiticity of `Γ` is *not* needed, see below), and a unitary involution `R` with `[R,W] = [R,Γ] = 0`. Key algebra: `C := ΓW` satisfies `C² = ΓWΓW = WᴴW = 1`, so **`W = Γ·C` is a product of two involutions commuting with `R`**. For each sector projector `P_± = (1 ± R)/2`, define

```
ν₀(±) := ½ · tr( (Γ + ΓW) P_± ) ∈ ℤ ,   ν_π(±) := ½ · tr( (Γ − ΓW) P_± ) ∈ ℤ .
```

Integrality: traces of involutions on a `d`-dim space are integers `≡ d (mod 2)`, so the half-sum/difference are integers. This is the finite closed-loop avatar of Asboth–Obuse's `(ν₀, ν_π)` (arXiv:1303.1199) — on a closed loop there is no quasimomentum winding, and what survives of their invariant is exactly the timeframe trace index, here refined by the dihedral reflection. [comp]/[interp]

### (b) Theorem — sectored chiral pinning (grade: M-target; inequality is spectral-theorem-free)

> **Theorem.** In each `R`-sector `V_χ`: `dim(ker(W−1) ∩ V_χ) ≥ |ν₀(χ)|` and `dim(ker(W+1) ∩ V_χ) ≥ |ν_π(χ)|`. Hence `mult_W(+1) ≥ Σ_χ |ν₀(χ)|`, `mult_W(−1) ≥ Σ_χ |ν_π(χ)|`.

*Proof (finite linear algebra only).* Restrict to `V_χ` (everything commutes with `R`). `Γ, C` are involutions, so over ℂ (char 0) `V_χ = ker(Γ−1) ⊕ ker(Γ+1)`, with `p := dim ker(Γ−1) = (d + tr Γ|_χ)/2`, likewise `p'` for `C`. If `Γv = v, Cv = v` then `Wv = ΓCv = v`; if `Γv = −v, Cv = −v` then `Wv = Γ(−v) = v`. The two intersections lie in different `Γ`-eigenspaces, so they sum directly inside `ker(W−1)`, and `dim ≥ max(0, p+p'−d) + max(0, d−p−p') ≥ |p + p' − d| = |ν₀(χ)|` by `Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`. Swap `C → −C` for `ν_π`. ∎

Mathlib route: eigenspaces as ranges of the idempotents `(1 ± Γ)/2`; `LinearMap.IsProj.trace` (trace of projection = finrank, exists) converts traces to dimensions; the dimension formula does the rest. **No spectral theorem, no Hermiticity of `Γ`** — the existing `ChiralInvolution` structure plus `Wᴴ W = 1` and the commuting `R` suffice. (Refinement `mult ≡ ν (mod 2)` per sector needs the full Halmos two-involution block decomposition — grade that separately, MEMO.)

### (c) The half-winding computation (verified today; makes a decide-style fixture)

`Γ = 1_V ⊗ σ_x` (orientation swap, `tr Γ = 0`); `R` = leg-reflection ∘ orientation swap; `[W,R] = 0` exactly (also for any *palindromic* per-leg amplitude pattern `t_ℓ = t_{−ℓ−1}`; verified with `[0.3,0.6,0.6,0.3]`, pinning intact `(2,2)`). Measured: `tr(ΓW P_±) = 0`, so all four invariants collapse to a single geometric integer:

```
ν₀(±) = ν_π(±) = ± ¼ · tr(Γ R) ,   and  ΓR = bare leg-reflection ⇒ tr(ΓR) = 2 · #{fixed legs} = 4  (even V: legs 0 and V/2).
```

So `ν₀(±) = ν_π(±) = ±1` ⇒ **≥ 1 pinned `+1` and ≥ 1 pinned `−1` per sector ⇒ mult(+1), mult(−1) ≥ 2** — exactly the observed `(2,2)` at every `|t|`, V = 4, 6, 8. The `|t|`-independence is now structural, not mysterious: the invariant `¼ tr(ΓR)` **does not involve `W` at all** — it is the fixed-point count of the reflection (a Lefschetz number), pure decoration geometry. `W` enters only through the two commutation hypotheses.

**Discriminating controls (run today):** (i) per-leg `|t| = [0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9]` keeps chirality *exact* (defect ~1e-15) but breaks `R` → pinning destroyed, `mult = (0,0)`, `min|ev∓1| ≈ 0.1` — chirality alone provably insufficient, matching the vanishing global index; (ii) palindromic nonuniform `|t|` keeps `R` → `(2,2)` intact. The mechanism passed both directions of its own falsifier.

### (d) Pre-registered kill conditions

- **K-C4a (fixture):** exact rational fixture `V = 4`, `t = 3/5`, `f = 4/5`, alternating phases (`W` is a real matrix — verified — so the fixture is rational): verify sector indices `(±1,±1)` and `mult(±1) = 2` by exact arithmetic. KILL the invariant if any chiral, `R`-symmetric decoration has all sector indices 0 yet exact pinning on an open `|t|` interval (invariant incomplete), or `|ν(χ)| = 1` with no pinned mode in that sector (theorem false).
- **K-C4b (independence):** chirality-preserving, `R`-breaking families must never pin exactly on an interval. Passed today; keep as a standing regression.
- **K-C4c (odd V consistency):** half-winding requires even `V`; predict no member of this family at odd `V` carries both symmetries with nonzero index. A counterexample with fractional "index" would mean misidentified `R`.

Grades: (a) definition M-target; (b) inequality M-target (route above), parity refinement MEMO; (c) numeric-oracle-verified today, fixture is a decide-style M-target; AO identification [comp]/[interp]; global-invariant impossibility for this decoration: measured fact (oracle).

## Part C — the three highest-leverage next targets

**#1 — (ii) Total-operator positivity on the doublet-free complement.** This moves the honest-claim frontier most because it is the program-wide bottleneck, not one lane's: P6 embargoes spectral language *everywhere* until it resolves. S1-CC's resolution made its hypotheses well-posed for the first time — closure is balanced, i.e. a *bounded signed* perturbation, and the question is whether the aperture+turn channels dominate it on the complement. Landing it converts every "eigenvalue-count identity" into an honest "mass = eigenvalue of a positive operator on the physical sector," gives the Banks–Casher count its physical reading, and is the *precondition* for S5. Note the beautiful closing of the circle: the dominance constant is the aperture gap — the trusted-core `det P` pairwise-disagreement invariant becomes the positivity budget. Concrete first theorem (three-line proof, house-style; the physics then lives in two follow-up rungs):

```lean
/-- Aperture dominance rung: a channel split A + C, with A bounded below by
c > 0 on the doublet-free complement P and the balanced channel C
Cauchy-Schwarz-bounded by kappa < c there, is positive-definite on P. -/
theorem aperture_dominance_pos (A C : Matrix n n ℂ) (P : Submodule ℂ (n → ℂ))
    (c κ : ℝ) (hκc : κ < c)
    (hA : ∀ v ∈ P, c * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (star v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v).re)
    (hC : ∀ v ∈ P, |(star v ⬝ᵥ C.mulVec v).re| ≤ κ * ‖v‖ ^ 2) :
    ∀ v ∈ P, v ≠ 0 → 0 < (star v ⬝ᵥ (A + C).mulVec v).re
```

Rung 2: `κ ≤ ‖bivector‖·‖K‖` for the closure channel (submultiplicativity). Rung 3: compute `c` and `κ` on the 6×6 S1-CC witness by rational arithmetic — the first kernel-checked total-operator positivity witness on a physical sector. Then the general Weyl eigenvalue-shift refinement as an Aristotle package (Weyl inequalities are likely absent from Mathlib — a genuine contribution).

**#2 — (iv) S6 mass-budget on a genuine color-singlet.** The manuscript headline currently rests on a single-edge witness; "hadron mass is mostly aperture+closure" is only honest evaluated on a strand-monomial singlet state. It is unblocked *now* (a budget is a decomposition of a number, needing no positivity), pure finite linear algebra in the exterior-algebra color fiber, and it will honestly exhibit the *sign structure* the balanced closure channel predicts (hyperfine-like, pi/rho-analog splitting, per P2) — a claim upgrade and a prediction in one.

**#3 — (iii) S5 first-meson witness, sequenced after #1.** With positivity on the complement, the already-kernel-checked OS/transfer gap turns a color-singlet two-point function into "a hadron-shaped correlator decays at the mass-gap rate" — the first honest finite hadron-mass statement. I rank it above (i) KP deliberately: KP adds uniformity-in-β to a gap the program already possesses on concrete lattices — five failed expert attempts say its marginal cost is extreme while its marginal honest-mass claim is small. Demote KP to a standing Aristotle bounty, not a lane. Under (v): tonight's Part B result hints the deeper unifier is an *equivariant index theory on decorated complexes* (McKean–Singer, the C4 sectored pinning, and the S1-CC constraint-compatible grading are all instances) — a program note, not a next move.

NOT a Lean result.\nUsage: python Scripts/oracle/p1_zeromode_symmetry_invariant.py\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom p1_zero_mode_locus_scan import transfer_from_data\n\nRNG = np.random.default_rng(20260708)\n\n\ndef symmetric_data(v, t_abs, winding, phi0=0.0):\n    \"\"\"Uniform |t|, winding flip phases: the symmetric-cone gauge data.\"\"\"\n    return t_abs, [phi0 + 2.0 * np.pi * winding * leg / v for leg in range(v)]\n\n\ndef cyclic_shift(v):\n    \"\"\"Bare leg-shift S on the 2V-dim (leg, orientation) space, +1 leg.\"\"\"\n    s = np.zeros((2 * v, 2 * v), dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        for orient in (0, 1):\n            s[2 * ((leg + 1) % v) + orient, 2 * leg + orient] = 1.0\n    return s\n\n\ndef dressed_shift(v, alpha):\n    \"\"\"Phase-dressed shift: S times diag phase e^{i alpha * leg} per leg.\"\"\"\n    s = cyclic_shift(v)\n    d = np.diag([np.exp(1j * alpha * leg)\n                 for leg in range(v) for _ in (0, 1)])\n    return s @ d\n\n\ndef find_symmetry(w, v):\n    \"\"\"Return an order-V unitary S commuting with W (bare or dressed).\"\"\"\n    for alpha in [0.0] + [2 * np.pi * k / v for k in range(v)]:\n        s = dressed_shift(v, alpha)\n        if np.linalg.norm(w @ s - s @ w) < 1e-9:\n            return s, alpha\n    # last resort: search a continuous dressing phase\n    best, bestval = None, 1e9\n    for alpha in np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 400, endpoint=False):\n        s = dressed_shift(v, alpha)\n        val = np.linalg.norm(w @ s - s @ w)\n        if val < bestval:\n            best, bestval, besta = s, val, alpha\n    return (best, besta) if bestval < 1e-6 else (None, None)\n\n\ndef sector_analysis(w, s, v):\n    \"\"\"Project W onto S-eigenspaces; per sector report dim, det, pinning.\"\"\"\n    svals, svecs = np.linalg.eig(s)\n    # group eigenvectors by S-eigenvalue (the cyclic sector label)\n    order = np.argsort(np.angle(svals))\n    svals, svecs = svals[order], svecs[:, order]\n    sectors = []\n    used = np.zeros(len(svals), bool)\n    for i in range(len(svals)):\n        if used[i]:\n            continue\n        grp = [j for j in range(len(svals))\n               if abs(np.angle(svals[j] / svals[i])) < 1e-6]\n        for j in grp:\n            used[j] = True\n        basis = svecs[:, grp]\n        basis, _ = np.linalg.qr(basis)  # orthonormalize the sector\n        wsec = basis.conj().T @ w @ basis\n        ev = np.linalg.eigvals(wsec)\n        pinned = np.min(np.abs(ev - 1.0)) < 1e-7 or \\\n            np.min(np.abs(ev + 1.0)) < 1e-7\n        det = np.linalg.det(wsec)\n        sectors.append(dict(slabel=np.angle(svals[i]), dim=basis.shape[1],\n                            det=det, pinned=pinned, ev=ev))\n    return sectors\n\n\ndef has_reciprocal_pairing(ev, tol=1e-6):\n    \"\"\"Spectrum closed under lambda -> 1/lambda (= conj on unit circle).\"\"\"\n    ev = list(ev)\n    for lam in ev:\n        if abs(abs(lam) - 1) > 1e-6:\n            return False\n        if not any(abs(mu - np.conj(lam)) < tol for mu in ev):\n            return False\n    return True\n\n\ndef run(v, t_abs, winding, label):\n    t, fph = symmetric_data(v, t_abs, winding)\n    w = transfer_from_data(v, t, 0.0, fph)  # holonomy folded into fph winding\n    unit_defect = np.linalg.norm(w.conj().T @ w - np.eye(2 * v))\n    s, alpha = find_symmetry(w, v)\n    ev_all = np.linalg.eigvals(w)\n    pinned_global = np.min(np.abs(ev_all - 1.0)) < 1e-7\n    print(f\"=== {label}: V={v} |t|={t_abs:.3f} winding={winding} ===\")\n    print(f\"  W unitary defect {unit_defect:.1e}; global unit eigenvalue \"\n          f\"pinned: {pinned_global} (min|ev-1|={np.min(np.abs(ev_all-1)):.1e})\")\n    if s is None:\n        print(\"  NO commuting cyclic symmetry found (Q1 FAIL)\")\n        return\n    print(f\"  Q1: commuting symmetry S found, dressing alpha={alpha:.4f}, \"\n          f\"[W,S]={np.linalg.norm(w@s-s@w):.1e}\")\n    secs = sector_analysis(w, s, v)\n    for sec in secs:\n        recip = has_reciprocal_pairing(sec['ev'])\n        detreal = abs(sec['det'].imag) < 1e-6\n        print(f\"  sector s={sec['slabel']:+.3f}: dim={sec['dim']} \"\n              f\"pinned={sec['pinned']} det={sec['det']:+.3f} \"\n              f\"(|det|={abs(sec['det']):.3f}, real={detreal}) \"\n              f\"reciprocal={recip}\")\n    # Q5 falsifier check: does (pinned) <=> (a sector has a real det with\n    # the reciprocal structure and forced eigenvalue)?\n    pin_sectors = [sec for sec in secs if sec['pinned']]\n    print(f\"  -> {len(pin_sectors)} pinned sector(s); \"\n          f\"pinning lives at sector label(s) \"\n          f\"{[round(sec['slabel'],3) for sec in pin_sectors]}\")\n\n\ndef break_symmetry_test(v, t_abs, winding):\n    \"\"\"Q4: perturb ONE leg's flip phase; does exact pinning survive?\"\"\"\n    t, fph = symmetric_data(v, t_abs, winding)\n    print(f\"=== Q4 symmetry-breaking (V={v}, |t|={t_abs:.3f}) ===\")\n    for eps in (0.0, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1):\n        fph2 = list(fph)\n        fph2[0] += eps\n        w = transfer_from_data(v, t, 0.0, fph2)\n        d = np.min(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvals(w) - 1.0))\n        print(f\"  eps={eps:.0e}: min|ev-1| = {d:.2e} \"\n              f\"({'EXACT pin' if d < 1e-7 else 'drifted'})\")\n\n\ndef main():\n    inv_t = 1.0 / np.sqrt(3.0)\n    for v in (3, 4, 5):\n        run(v, inv_t, 1, \"symmetric winding-1\")\n    run(4, 0.5, 2, \"symmetric even-V half-winding\")\n    print()\n    break_symmetry_test(3, inv_t, 1)\n    break_symmetry_test(4, 0.5, 2)\n    # Q5 broad falsifier sweep: random symmetric decorations, does the\n    # equivariant premise + a pinned sector always co-occur with a global\n    # unit eigenvalue?\n    print(\"\\n=== Q5 falsifier sweep (random symmetric decorations) ===\")\n    bad = 0\n    for _ in range(40):\n        v = int(RNG.integers(3, 7))\n        t_abs = float(RNG.uniform(0.2, 0.95))\n        winding = int(RNG.integers(0, v))\n        t, fph = symmetric_data(v, t_abs, winding)\n        w = transfer_from_data(v, t, 0.0, fph)\n        pinned = np.min(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvals(w) - 1.0)) < 1e-7 or \\\n            np.min(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvals(w) + 1.0)) < 1e-7\n        s, _ = find_symmetry(w, v)\n        equivariant = s is not None\n        if equivariant and not pinned:\n            bad += 1\n            print(f\"  FALSIFIER: V={v} |t|={t_abs:.3f} w={winding} \"\n                  f\"equivariant but NOT pinned\")\n    print(f\"  falsifiers found: {bad}/40 \"\n          f\"({'mechanism SURVIVES' if bad == 0 else 'mechanism NEEDS REVISION'})\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n","numLines":200,"startLine":1,"totalLines":200}}}

For each (V, w, |t|), sweep h and locate\n  zero-mode crossings h*(|t|). THE question: is h* independent of |t|\n  (topological - the Berry phase alone forces the massless mode) or not\n  (fine-tuned)? The overall flip phase is a proven unitary-equivalence and\n  is fixed to 0.\n\nNumeric oracle only; NOT a Lean result. t_abs^2) with per-corner phases f_phases[leg].\n    \"\"\"\n    f_abs = np.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - t_abs ** 2))\n    t = t_abs * np.exp(1j * h / v)\n    w = np.zeros((2 * v, 2 * v), dtype=complex)\n\n    def idx(leg, s):\n        return 2 * (leg % v) + s\n\n    for leg in range(v):\n        f = f_abs * np.exp(1j * f_phases[leg])\n        w[idx(leg + 1, 0), idx(leg, 0)] = t\n        w[idx(leg + 1, 0), idx(leg + 1, 1)] = -np.conj(f)\n        w[idx(leg, 1), idx(leg, 0)] = f\n        w[idx(leg, 1), idx(leg + 1, 1)] = np.conj(t)\n    return w\n\n\ndef min_abs_phase(w):\n    \"\"\"Distance of the spectrum from eigenvalue 1 (zero quasi-energy).\"\"\"\n    return float(np.min(np.abs(np.angle(np.linalg.eigvals(w)))))\n\n\ndef min_pi_phase(w):\n    \"\"\"Distance of the spectrum from eigenvalue -1 (pi quasi-energy).\"\"\"\n    ph = np.angle(np.linalg.eigvals(w))\n    return float(np.min(np.abs(np.abs(ph) - np.pi)))\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- SCAN A\n\ndef spinor_of_direction(n):\n    n = np.asarray(n, dtype=float)\n    n = n / np.linalg.norm(n)\n    theta = np.arccos(np.clip(n[2], -1.0, 1.0))\n    phi = np.arctan2(n[1], n[0])\n    return np.array([np.cos(theta / 2.0),\n                     np.exp(1j * phi) * np.sin(theta / 2.0)])\n\n\ndef corner_amplitudes(psi_in, psi_out):\n    t = np.vdot(psi_out, psi_in)\n    f = psi_in[0] * psi_out[1] - 1):\n        beta[leg + 1] = beta[leg] + np.angle(ts[leg]) - h / v\n    f_phases = [np.angle(fs[leg]) + beta[leg] + beta[(leg + 1) % v]\n                for leg in range(v)]\n    t_abs = abs(ts[0])\n    return transfer_from_data(v, t_abs, h, f_phases), h, t_abs\n\n\ndef scan_a():\n    print(\"=== SCAN A: symmetric V-gon on a cone, sweep half-angle chi ===\")\n    for v in (3, 4, 5, 6):\n        chis = np.linspace(0.02, np.pi - 0.02, 1201)\n        g = np.array([min_abs_phase(cone_case(v, c)[0]) for c in chis])\n        # find deep local minima and refine by ternary search\n        hits = []\n        for i in range(1, len(chis) - {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5","id":"msg_011CcpB2zdHNp9aCpXeDd58T","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VSMHvdmMCYvnR3Rc2SPBuH","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd Scripts/oracle && python -c \"\nimport numpy as np\nfrom p1_zero_mode_locus_scan import transfer_from_data\n\ndef gamma_swap(v):\n    g = np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        g[2*leg,2*leg+1]=1.0; g[2*leg+1,2*leg]=1.0\n    return g\n\nfor v in (4,6,8):\n    for t_abs in (0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9):\n        fph=[2.0*np.pi*(v//2)*leg/v for leg in range(v)]  # half-winding\n        w=transfer_from_data(v,t_abs,0.0,fph)\n        g=gamma_swap(v)\n        chiral=np.linalg.norm(g@w@g - w.conj().T)\n        herm=np.linalg.norm(g-g.conj().T)\n        c1=g@w\n        c1herm=np.linalg.norm(c1-c1.conj().T)\n        c1sq=np.linalg.norm(c1@c1-np.eye(2*v))\n        trG=np.trace(g).real; trGW=np.trace(c1).real\n        nu0=0.5*(trG+trGW); nupi=0.5*(trG-trGW)\n        ev=np.linalg.eigvals(w)\n        m1=np.sum(np.abs(ev-1)<1e-7); mm1=np.sum(np.abs(ev+1)<1e-7)\n        print(f'V={v} |t|={t_abs}: chiral_defect={chiral:.1e} GW-herm={c1herm:.1e} (GW)^2-1={c1sq:.1e} trGamma={trG:+.3f} trGW={trGW:+.4f} nu0={nu0:+.3f} nupi={nupi:+.3f} mult(+1)={m1} mult(-1)={mm1}'\n)\n\"","description":"Compute trace index nu0, nupi for half-winding decoration"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1448,"cache_read_input_tokens":58729,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1448,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3c82d87d-232b-45df-9ef6-1d82e7b5b34c","uuid":"1bdbaabd-5b85-4b25-b0ee-db6f205c9efe"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5","id":"msg_011CcpB5mHSbhrmH34qKdd12","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XDDiB9KDePNfSduqSHogJ4","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd Scripts/oracle && python -c \"\nimport numpy as np\nfrom p1_zero_mode_locus_scan import transfer_from_data\nfrom p1_zeromode_symmetry_invariant import find_symmetry\n\ndef gamma_swap(v):\n    g=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        g[2*leg,2*leg+1]=1.0; g[2*leg+1,2*leg]=1.0\n    return g\n\nfor v,t_abs in [(4,0.5),(4,0.8),(6,0.35),(8,0.62)]:\n    fph=[2.0*np.pi*(v//2)*leg/v for leg in range(v)]\n    w=transfer_from_data(v,t_abs,0.0,fph)\n    g=gamma_swap(v)\n    s,alpha=find_symmetry(w,v)\n    print(f'--- V={v} |t|={t_abs}: dressing alpha={alpha:.4f}, [W,S]={np.linalg.norm(w@s-s@w):.1e}, [Gamma,S]={np.linalg.norm(g@s-s@g):.1e}')\n    # also check Gamma S Gamma = S^{-1}? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5","id":"msg_011CcpB99qLkrfxhdZHCbYwY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018LJ7Q1LhPjbijWhNpiKA4w","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python -c \"\nimport numpy as np\nfrom p1_zero_mode_locus_scan import transfer_from_data\n\ndef gamma_swap(v):\n    g=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        g[2*leg,2*leg+1]=1.0; g[2*leg+1,2*leg]=1.0\n    return g\n\nv,t_abs=4,0.5\nfph=[2.0*np.pi*(v//2)*leg/v for leg in range(v)]\nw=transfer_from_data(v,t_abs,0.0,fph)\ng=gamma_swap(v)\nn=2*v\n# 1) is W real? (PH in standard basis)\nprint('||W - conj(W)|| =', np.linalg.norm(w-w.conj()))\n# 2) shift by ONE leg: S W S^-1 vs W and -W and W with phase\ndef shift(v,orient_phases=None):\n    s=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        for o in (0,1):\n            s[2*((leg+1)%v)+o,2*leg+o]=1.0\n    return s\ns=shift(v)\nsw=s@w@s.conj().T\n# compare sw to w up to a diagonal-phase gauge? check |entries| pattern\nprint('||SWS^-1 - W|| =',np.linalg.norm(sw-w), ' ||SWS^-1 + W|| =',np.linalg.norm(sw+w))\n# 3) two-leg shift\ns2=s@s\nprint('||S2WS2^-1 - W|| =',np.linalg.norm(s2@w@s2.conj().T-w))\n# 4) shift with orientation-dependent phases: S_d = shift * diag(e^{i a leg} on o=0, e^{i b leg} on o=1)\nfound=[]\nfor a in np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,9,endpoint=False):\n    for b in np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,9,endpoint=False):\n        d=np.diag([np.exp(1j*(a*leg if o==0 else b*leg)) for leg in range(v) for o in (0,1)])\n        sd=s@d\n        if np.linalg.norm(sd@w-w@sd)<1e-9: found.append((a,b))\nprint('orientation-dressed commuting shifts:',found[:5])\n# 5) reflection: leg -> -leg mod v, orientation swap, with optional phases\nr=np.zeros((n,n),dtype=complex)\nfor leg in range(v):\n    for o in (0,1):\n        r[2*((-leg)%v)+(1-o),2*leg+o]=1.0\nprint('reflection+oswap: ||RWR^-1 - W|| =',np.linalg.norm(r@w@np.linalg.inv(r)-w),' vs W^dag:',np.linalg.norm(r@w@np.linalg.inv(r)-w.conj().T))\nr2=np.zeros((n,n),dtype=complex)\nfor leg in range(v):\n    for o in (0,1):\n        r2[2*((-leg)%v)+o,2*leg+o]=1.0\nprint('reflection only:  ||RWR^-1 - W|| =',np.linalg.norm(r2@w@np.linalg.inv(r2)-w),' vs W^dag:',np.linalg.norm(r2@w@np.linalg.inv(r2)-w.conj().T),' vs conj(W):',np.linalg.norm(r2@w@np.linalg.inv(r2)-w.conj()))\n# 6) eigenvalues and (GW) spectral structure on pinned spaces\nev,evec=np.linalg.eig(w)\nfor lam in (1.0,-1.0):\n    idx=[i for i in range(n) if abs(ev[i]-lam)<1e-7]\n    P=evec[:,idx]; does R break? pinning?\ncases=[('uniform',[0.5]*4),('palindromic-ish',[0.3,0.6,0.3,0.6]),('non-palin',[0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9]),('non-palin2',[0.2,0.9,0.4,0.6])]\nfor name,tl in cases:\n    w=transfer_perleg(v,tl,fph)\n    chir=np.linalg.norm(g@w@g-w.conj().T)\n    commR=np.linalg.norm(w@r-r@w)\n    ev=np.linalg.eigvals(w)\n    d1=np.min(np.abs(ev-1)); dm1=np.min(np.abs(ev+1))\n    m1=int(np.sum(np.abs(ev-1)<1e-7)); mm1=int(np.sum(np.abs(ev+1)<1e-7))\n    print(f'{name}: chiral={chir:.1e} [W,R]={commR:.1e} min|ev-1|={d1:.2e} min|ev+1|={dm1:.2e} mult=({m1},{mm1})')\n\"","description":"Chiral-preserving R-breaking family via per-leg amplitudes"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5881,"cache_read_input_tokens":74970,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":5881,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3c82d87d-232b-45df-9ef6-1d82e7b5b34c","uuid":"ec3bf210-a37b-47b3-b5f5-c0b9c9c88db7"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5","id":"msg_011CcpBLNeLG31BzgZ91GWGE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Kh3MWQszcfYUFJNK1Rs78G","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python -c \"\nimport numpy as np\n\ndef transfer_perleg(v,t_list,fph):\n    w=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    def idx(leg,s): return 2*(leg%v)+s\n    for leg in range(v):\n        t=t_list[leg]; f=np.sqrt(max(0.0,1.0-abs(t)**2))*np.exp(1j*fph[leg])\n        w[idx(leg+1,0),idx(leg,0)]=t\n        w[idx(leg+1,0),idx(leg+1,1)]=-np.conj(f)\n        w[idx(leg,1),idx(leg,0)]=f\n        w[idx(leg,1),idx(leg+1,1)]=np.conj(t)\n    return w\n\ndef gamma_swap(v):\n    g=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n    for leg in range(v):\n        g[2*leg,2*leg+1]=1.0; g[2*leg+1,2*leg]=1.0\n    return g\n\nv=4\ng=gamma_swap(v)\nfph=[2.0*np.pi*(v//2)*leg/v for leg in range(v)]\n# search reflection center c: leg -> (c - leg) mod v, with orientation swap\npatterns=[('t_l=t_{-l-1}',[0.3,0.6,0.6,0.3]),('t_l=t_{1-l}',[0.6,0.3,0.6,0.3]),('t_l=t_{2-l}? ',[0.3,0.6,0.9,0.6])]\nfor name,tl in patterns:\n    w=transfer_perleg(v,tl,fph)\n    best=None\n    for c in range(v):\n        r=np.zeros((2*v,2*v),dtype=complex)\n        for leg in range(v):\n            for o in (0,1): r[2*((c-leg)%v)+(1-o),2*leg+o]=1.0\n        cr=np.linalg.norm(w@r-r@w)\n        if best is None or cr<best[1]: best=(c,cr,r)\n    c,cr,r=best\n    chir=np.linalg.norm(g@w@g-w.conj().T)\n    ev=np.linalg.eigvals(w)\n    m1=int(np.sum(np.abs(ev-1)<1e-7)); mm1=int(np.sum(np.abs(ev+1)<1e-7))\n    trGR=np.trace(g@r).real\n    print(f'{name}: chiral={chir:.1e} best center c={c} [W,R_c]={cr:.1e} tr(Gamma R)={trGR:+.1f} mult=({m1},{mm1}) min|ev-1|={np.min(np.abs(ev-1)):.1e}')\n\"","description":"Find R-preserving nonuniform positive control"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1623,"cache_read_input_tokens":80851,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1623,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3c82d87d-232b-45df-9ef6-1d82e7b5b34c","uuid":"6bde1a78-f196-499b-b7c3-da4969bdaaa3"}
